feature: Pen pressure, tilt and speed, and the mouse taper
summary: Every brush now answers the hand: a pen pressed harder paints wider and darker where that medium would, leaning it lays charcoal and chalk on their side and turns a chisel marker, and a fast stroke thins. A mouse stroke swells in from a point and tapers out instead of starting and ending as a blunt circle.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. No tablet was attached to the test Mac: the pen strokes here are synthetic pressure and tilt fed through the same placement and rasterizer a tablet's samples take (walk 'pen-pressure-and-mouse-taper-walk', and the sheet from PHOTONZ_DYNAMICS_SHEET=<dir> Scripts/test.sh --filter DynamicsSheet).

try.do: Open a blank image, press B, and pick Charcoal from the brush tiles over the tool bar.
Drag a line with the mouse and let go: it starts from a point, swells to the Size, and its end draws in to a point as it lands.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: With a tablet or an Apple Pencil through Sidecar, draw one line pressing lightly and one pressing hard: light is thin and grey, hard is broad and black.
Lean the pen well over and drag across: charcoal lays a broad, paler band with the side of the stick.
Pick Marker, set Tip to Chisel, and draw with the pen leaned two different ways: the nib's broad edge turns with the lean.
Draw the same line slowly and then quickly: the quick one is thinner.

evaluate: Does the mouse taper feel natural, or does the end drawing in as the stroke lands catch your eye?
With a real pen, is the steady middle press about the width the ring under the pointer shows?
Is the heavy press on charcoal and watercolour too wide (up to about 1.3 times the Size)?
Does leaned charcoal read as the side of the stick, and is chalk's side broad enough?
Should the marker taper at all with a mouse, or start and end as a full round nib like a real felt tip?
rough: No tablet was attached to the test Mac, so nothing here was drawn with a real pen; pen strokes are synthetic samples through the same path a tablet's take (the task's own acceptance item).

The end of a mouse stroke thins only when the button comes up: the live stroke cannot know where it ends, so the last few tip widths draw in as the stroke lands (the walk measured 0.13% of the canvas changing). Chose that over replaying the stroke at release or holding the tail back while drawing (docs/design/brushes.md, What the dynamics settled).

Size is the width at the mouse's steady press, not at a full press as in Photoshop, so a hard press paints up to about 1.3 times the Size, past the ring under the pointer. Chose it so a mouse paints exactly what the ring shows.
The airbrush has no taper (its spray already feathers) and its press stays its flow; the pencil keeps its own press and lean and gains the taper and pen-speed thinning.
No mock covers the pressure response; the design doc's decision 6 is the spec.

No reel: what changes is the shape of a stroke, shown on the stroke sheet (light, medium, heavy, swell, leaned, mouse slow, mouse fast for each of the eight brushes), with its numbers in 2026-10-25-pen-pressure-measures.txt.
